sources.entry: Beaker Browser - Beaker is an experimental peer-to-peer Web browser.

summary.one_liner: Beaker is an archived experimental peer-to-peer web browser built on Electron that adds APIs for hostless applications.
summary.what_it_does: The README states Beaker was an experimental peer-to-peer Web browser that added new APIs for building hostless applications while staying compatible with the regular Web. The project is now archived, so it is no longer under active development. The README covers building from source (Node 12+, with platform-specific native build prerequisites for Linux, macOS and Windows) and running it with npm scripts. It documents environment variables for log output (DEBUG), opening a URL on load (BEAKER_OPEN_URL), overriding the user-data path (BEAKER_USER_DATA_PATH), and the default storage quota for dat sites (BEAKER_DAT_QUOTA_DEFAULT_BYTES_ALLOWED, default 500mb). It also notes a known macOS startup hang when launched from tmux and points to SECURITY.md for vulnerability reporting. Binaries are provided via the Releases page.
use_cases: Testing dat-based sites with custom storage quotas
Running a developer build of an experimental browser
how_to_run: Install Node 12 or higher, plus platform build tools (libtool, m4, autoconf, automake on Linux/macOS; Python 2.7, Visual Studio and Git on Windows)
notable: Hostless application APIs layered on top of normal Web compatibility
Peer-to-peer content via dat sites with configurable storage quotas
Environment variables for debug logging and user-data path override
Ships binaries on a Releases page; source build is also documented
caveats: Project is archived and no longer maintained
Building from source requires platform-specific native toolchains; Windows needs older Python 2.7 and Visual Studio 2015/2017
Known startup hang on macOS when launched from tmux
